h1: 5 KB photo size: compress image to 5 KB
intro: Need the 5 KB photo size for a tiny upload field? Add your picture and get a JPG between 4.5 and 5 KB, made on your phone with nothing uploaded.

steps.name: Add your image
steps.text: Take a photo or pick one from your gallery. JPG, PNG, WebP and iPhone HEIC files all work.

steps.name: Check the target
steps.text: 5 KB is already selected. Type a minimum if your form sets one, and decide whether the pixel size may change.

steps.name: Let it work
steps.text: The tool tries the highest JPEG quality that stays under 5 KB and makes the picture smaller only when it has to.

steps.name: Download
steps.text: When every line of the pass check has a tick, save the JPG and upload it to your form.

faq.q: Can a passport photo really be 5 KB?
faq.a: Yes, but only at a small pixel size, around 90×120. If your form allows 10 or 20 KB, use that instead: the face will be noticeably sharper.

faq.q: The portal says "less than 5 KB". Is 4.9 KB safe?
faq.a: Yes. The file lands between 4.5 and 5 KB and stays under 5,000 bytes, so it passes whether the portal counts a kilobyte as 1000 or 1024 bytes.

faq.q: Why did my picture get so small in pixels?
faq.a: A 12-megapixel phone photo cannot fit in 5 KB at full size, so the tool shrinks it step by step until the quality is acceptable. Turn on Keep dimensions only if the form fixes the width and height.

sections.h2: Where a 5 KB limit shows up
paras: Five kilobytes is rare on national exam forms, and none of the exams we track uses it as a maximum. You meet it on older state, university and scholarship portals built when storage was expensive, usually for a signature or a small ID photo. It also helps when a form gives a very low floor: CTET accepts a signature from 3 KB up to 30 KB, so a 5 KB copy of your signature fits.

At 5 KB there is room for a face about the size of a postage stamp on screen. Skin turns smooth and hair loses its strands, but the face stays recognisable at the size portals display it. A dark-ink signature on white paper survives much better: the white area costs almost nothing, so the strokes stay clean.

As a rough guide, a passport-style photo on a plain background stays clean at about 90×120 pixels in 5 KB. A busy background or a dim, noisy shot needs more kilobytes for the same size, and a signature on white paper needs far fewer.

Whatever you add, the download is a baseline JPG (not progressive) between 4.5 and 5 KB. It stays under 5,000 bytes, so it passes whether the portal counts 1 KB as 1000 or 1024 bytes, and hidden camera and location data are removed.
Crop tightly first. For a photo keep only head and shoulders; for a signature cut the paper right up to the ink. Every pixel you remove is detail the 5 KB budget can spend on what matters.
Pick the size just under the limit printed on your form. If the form gives both a minimum and a maximum, a range page fills in the minimum for you.
